source_text: Ἔξεστι δὲ ἡμῖν ἐκ περιουσίας πρὸς τοὺς φιλεγκλήμονας ἐπαποδύσασθαι· οὐ γὰρ παῖδες ἡμεῖς καὶ νήπιοι πρὸς τὸ παιδαριῶδες καὶ εὐκαταφρόνητον τῆς μαθήσεως προσηγορεύμεθα, καθὼς οἱ εἰς γνῶσιν πεφυσιωμένοι διαβεβλήκασιν· ἀναγεννηθέντες γοῦν εὐθέως τὸ τέλειον ἀπειλήφαμεν, οὗ ἕνεκεν ἐσπεύδομεν. ἐφωτίσθημεν γάρ· τὸ δὲ ἔστιν ἐπιγνῶναι τὸν θεόν. οὔκουν ἀτελὴς ὁ ἐγνωκὼς τὸ τέλειον. καί μου μὴ λάβησθε ὁμολογοῦντος ἐγνωκέναι τὸν θεόν. ὧδέ πως γὰρ ἔδοξεν εἰπεῖν τῷ λόγῳ· ὃ δὲ ἐλεύθερος. αὐτίκα γοῦν βαπτιζομένῳ τῷ κυρίῳ ἀπ᾿ οὐρανῶν ἐπήχησε φωνὴ μάρτυς ἠγαπημένου »υἱός μου εἶ σὺ ἀγαπητός, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε.« πυθώμεθα οὖν τῶν σοφῶν· σήμερον ἀναγεννηθεὶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἤδη τέλειός ἐστιν ἤ, ὅπερ ἀτοπώτατον, ἐλλιπής. εἰ δὲ τοῦτο, προσμαθεῖν τι αὐτῷ δεῖ. ἀλλὰ προσμαθεῖν μὲν αὐτὸν εἰκὸς οὐδὲ ἓν θεὸν ὄντα. οὐ γὰρ ἂν μείζων τις εἴη τοῦ λόγου οὐδὲ μὴν διδάσκαλος τοῦ μόνου διδασκάλου. μή τι οὖν ὁμολογήσουσιν ἄκοντες τὸν λόγον, τέλειον ἐκ τελείου φύντα τοῦ πατρός, κατὰ τὴν οἰκονομικὴν προδιατύπωσιν ἀναγεννηθῆναι τελείως; καὶ εἰ τέλειος ἦν, τί ἐβαπτίζετο ὁ τέλειος; ἔδει, φασί, πληρῶσαι τὸ ἐπάγγελμα τὸ ἀνθρώπινον. παγκάλως. φημὶ γάρ· ἅμα τοίνυν τῷ βαπτίζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου γίνεται τέλειος; δῆλον ὅτι. οὐδὲν οὖν πρὸς αὐτοῦ προσέμαθεν; οὐ γάρ. τελειοῦται δὲ τῷ λουτρῷ μόνῳ καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῇ καθόδῳ ἁγιάζεται; οὕτως ἔχει. Τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ συμβαίνει τοῦτο καὶ περὶ ἡμᾶς, ὧν γέγονεν ὑπογραφὴ ὁ κύριος· βαπτιζόμενοι φωτιζόμεθα, φωτιζόμενοι υἱοποιούμεθα, υἱοποιούμενοι τελειούμεθα, τελειούμενοι ἀπαθανατιζόμεθα »ἐγώ«, φησίν, »εἶπα, θεοί ἐστε καὶ υἱοὶ ὑψίστου πάντες.« καλεῖται δὲ πολλαχῶς τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο, χάρισμα καὶ φώτισμα καὶ τέλειον καὶ λουτρόν· λουτρὸν μὲν δι᾿ οὗ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἀπορρυπτόμεθα, χάρισμα δὲ ᾧ τὰ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἁμαρτήμασιν ἐπιτίμια ἀνεῖται, φώτισμα δὲ δι᾿ οὗ τὸ ἅγιον ἐκεῖνο φῶς τὸ σωτήριον ἐποπτεύεται, τουτέστιν δι᾿ οὗ τὸ θεῖον ὀξυωποῦμεν, τέλειον δὲ τὸ ἀπροσδεὲς φαμέν. τί γὰρ ἔτι λείπεται τῷ θεὸν ἐγνωκότι; καὶ γὰρ ἄτοπον ὡς ἀληθῶς χάρισμα κεκλῆσθαι θεοῦ τὸ μὴ πεπληρωμένον· τέλειος δὲ ὢν τέλεια χαριεῖται δήπουθεν· ὡς δὲ ἅμα τῷ κελεῦσαι αὐτὸν πάντα γίνεται, οὕτως ἕπεται τῷ χαρίσασθαι μόνον βουληθῆναι αὐτὸν τὸ πεπληρῶσθαι τὴν χάριν. τὸ γὰρ μέλλον τοῦ χρόνου τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ θελήματος προλαμβάνεται. πρὸς δὲ καὶ ἡ τῶν κακῶν ἀπαλλαγὴ σωτηρίας ἐστὶν ἀρχή. μόνον δὲ ἄρα οἱ πρῶτον δραξάμενοι τῶν ὅρων τῆς ζωῆς ἤδη τέλειοι, ζῶμεν δὲ ἤδη οἱ θανάτου κεχωρισμένοι. σωτηρία τοίνυν τὸ ἕπεσθαι Χριστῷ. »ὃ γὰρ γέγονεν ἐν αὐτῷ, ζωή ἐστιν.« »ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν,« φησίν, »ὁ τὸν λόγον μου ἀκούων καὶ πιστεύων τῷ πέμψαντί με ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον καὶ εἰς κρίσιν οὐκ ἔρχεται, ἀλλὰ μεταβέβηκεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν.« οὕτω τὸ πιστεῦσαι μόνον καὶ ἀναγεννηθῆναι τελείωσίς ἐστιν ἐν ζωῇ· οὐ γάρ ποτε ἀσθενεῖ ὁ θεός.
pass_a_gloss: It is possible for us to divest ourselves of superfluity towards those who are fond of blame; for we are not children and infants in respect to the childish and easily despised thing of learning, as those who have been brought to knowledge have slandered; for having been reborn, we immediately received the perfect thing, on account of which we hasten. For we have been enlightened; and this is to know God. Therefore, the one who has known the perfect thing is not imperfect. And do not take hold of me as confessing that I have known God. For thus somehow it seemed right to the Word to speak; and what is free. Immediately, therefore, to the Lord being baptized from heaven, a voice sounded as a witness of the beloved: 'You are my Son, my beloved, today I have begotten you.' Let us learn, therefore, from the wise: today, having been reborn, is Christ already perfect or, which is absurd, imperfect? But if this, it is necessary for him to learn something. But it is fitting for him to learn nothing, being God. For no one would be greater than the Word, nor even a teacher of the only Teacher. Will they not, therefore, confess against their will that the Word, perfect from the perfect Father, was reborn perfectly according to the economic pre-arrangement? And if he was perfect, why was the perfect one baptized? It was necessary, they say, to fulfill the human promise. Beautifully, I say: for as soon as he was baptized by John, did he become perfect? Clearly. Did he, therefore, learn nothing in addition to this? No. For he is perfected by the bath alone and is sanctified by the descent of the Spirit. This is the case. The same thing happens to us, of whom the Lord has become a guarantee: being baptized, we are enlightened, being enlightened, we are made sons, being made sons, we are perfected, being perfected, we are made immortal. For He says, 'I have said, you are gods and all sons of the Most High.' And this work is called by many names: gift and enlightenment and perfect and bath; bath, indeed, through which we wash away sins, gift, by which the penalties for sins are remitted, enlightenment, through which that holy and saving light is beheld, that is, through which we perceive the divine, perfect, we say, what is without need. For what is still lacking to the one who has known God? And it is also absurd, indeed, for the gift of God to be called imperfect; but being perfect, he will surely give perfect gifts. For just as all things come into being as soon as he commands, so also it follows that when he gives, it is only necessary for him to will that the gift be fulfilled. For the future is anticipated by the power of his will. And the removal of evils is the beginning of salvation. Only, therefore, those who have first grasped the boundaries of life are already perfect, and we, having been separated from death, are already living. Salvation, therefore, is to follow Christ. 'For what has come into being in him is life.' 'Amen, amen, I say to you,' he says, 'the one who hears my word and believes in the one who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life.' Thus, to believe alone and to be reborn is perfection in life; for God is never weak.

pass_b_english: We are free to strip away all superfluous argument against those who love to find fault. We are not children or infants when it comes to the childish, easily dismissed kind of learning that those puffed up with knowledge have slandered us for. Having been reborn, we immediately received the perfect reality, the very thing we eagerly pursued. We have been enlightened—and enlightenment is nothing other than knowing God. Therefore, the one who has known the perfect is not imperfect. Do not hold it against me for confessing that I know God. For the Word saw fit to speak in just this way: "You are my Son, the Beloved; today I have begotten you" (Matthew 3:17)—and what the Word speaks is free. Immediately, as the Lord was baptized, a voice from heaven bore witness to the Beloved. Let us learn from the wise: was Christ already perfect the day he was reborn, or was he imperfect—which is absurd? If he were imperfect, he would have needed to learn something. But it is fitting that he learned nothing, because he is God. No one is greater than the Word, nor is anyone a teacher of the only Teacher. Will they not therefore confess, even against their will, that the Word, perfect from the perfect Father, was reborn perfectly according to the divine economy? If he was perfect, why was the perfect one baptized? They say it was necessary to fulfill the human promise. A beautiful answer. I say: did he become perfect the moment he was baptized by John? Obviously. Did he then learn anything additional? No. He is perfected by the bath alone and sanctified by the descent of the Spirit. That is how it stands. The same pattern holds for us; the Lord has become our guarantee. Being baptized, we are enlightened; being enlightened, we are adopted as sons; being adopted, we are perfected; being perfected, we are made immortal. "I said, you are gods, and all of you are sons of the Most High" (Psalm 82:6). This work is called by many names: gift, enlightenment, perfection, bath. Bath, because through it we wash away our sins; gift, because through it the penalties due for sins are remitted; enlightenment, because through it we behold that holy, saving light—that is, through it we perceive the divine. By "perfect" we mean what lacks nothing. What could still be lacking to the one who has known God? It would be absurd to call God's gift imperfect; being perfect, he surely gives perfect gifts. Just as all things come into being the moment he commands, so it follows that when he gives, he need only will that the gift be fulfilled. The future is anticipated by the power of his will. Even the removal of evils is the beginning of salvation. Only those who have first grasped the boundaries of life are already perfect—and we who have been separated from death are already alive. Salvation is to follow Christ. "What has come into being in him is life" (John 1:4). "Very truly, I tell you, whoever hears my word and believes in the one who sent me has eternal life and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life" (John 5:24). Thus, to believe and to be reborn is perfection in life; for God is never weak.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, while Pass B provides a fluent reading that correctly identifies and inserts the necessary scripture citations (Matthew 3:17, Psalm 82:6, John 1:4, John 5:24) which were alluded to in the Greek. All theological distinctions regarding the 'economic pre-arrangement' (οἰκονομικὴν προδιατύπωσιν) and the process of sanctification are preserved.
